notes: Full text read from the author manuscript on Archimer (Ifremer). Fermentative chemoorganoheterotroph; H2 is a fermentation product (butyrate, acetate, H2) and H2 was not tested as an electron donor. Sulfate is stated as not reduced in results and species description although it is not listed in the methods' acceptor list. acceptor_other (AQDS) positive is ambiguous: paper says the strain was 'facultatively dependent on' Fe(III) forms 'or AQDS as an electron shuttle'; Li et al. 2020 (Sci Total Environ) additionally show humic acids/riboflavin shuttle-mediated Fe(III) reduction. Formate negative comes from a carbon-source utilization list, not a dedicated electron-donor test. BacDive experimental oxygen tolerance 'anaerobe' agrees (its ML prediction 'facultative anaerobe' conflicts but is not experimental).

Electron acceptor tests used acetate as donor; donor tests used Fe(III)-NTA as acceptor. H2 and formate not tested in the protologue. Xu et al. 2024 mBio (PMC11633192) confirmed DNRA growth on nitrate and nitrite (Nap + NrfA, no Nar) and noted no nitrite oxidation to nitrate occurred in cultures (incidental observation, not a nitrite-oxidizer growth test, so donor_nitrite_oxidation left not_tested). Final SAM 2025 article (OA per Unpaywall) was blocked (HTTP 403); used Research Square preprint rs-4032669/v1 by same authors (protologue text) plus Hedlund et al. 2015 Front Microbiol (strain then called 'Hydrogenobacter sp. T-8'). Conflict: 2025 genus description states 'Cultivated members are capable of chemolithoheterotrophy using acetate', but Hedlund 2015 Table 3 lists acetate as a donor only for T-2, not T-8 (organic, not a scored category). 2025 methods also list S0, formate, formaldehyde, formamide and nitrite as tested for both strains; results per strain beyond the description were not visible in the preprint text. Genome encodes complete denitrification (narGH, nirS, norBC, nosZ) but N2O/N2 not detected experimentally. Arsenite oxidation not tested. Culture collection written 'CGMC 1.5214' in the preprint; LPSN gives CGMCC 1.5214.

notes: Full text PDF read (IJSEM bronze OA). The anaerobic-respiration negative sentence spans a column/page break in the PDF text ('The strain did not grow by fermentation of yeast extract or L-rhamnose' ... 'or anaerobic respiration with acetate ... NO3-, S2O32-, SO42- or Fe3+ as the electron acceptors'); reconstructed reading is unambiguous. Lithoautotrophic growth on siderite gives only modest yield increase over controls (without mineral 0.1-1.7x10^7 cells/ml) and no CO2-fixation pathway (no RubisCO) was identified; later paper (Palmer et al. 2023 ISME J, PMC10284905) notes 'no carbon fixation pathway was proposed' and sister species T. flava/T. thermophila are strictly aerobic. Hot in Cold review (PMC7565842, same group) confirms H2, soluble S compounds, ammonium, CO, nitrite could not replace siderite. CONFLICT: BacDive 167812 lists 'facultative anaerobe' but only as a machine-learning (BacteriaNet) prediction, contradicting the protologue's obligate aerobe. NCBI class 'Tepidiformia'; GTDB/Palmer et al. place lineage in Dehalococcoidia.

notes: Originally published as 'Thermoanaerosceptrum'; spelling corrected to Thermanaerosceptrum (LPSN), validated in IJSEM Validation List 198 (2021). Family Peptococcaceae. Electron acceptors (nitrite, nitrate, sulfate, sulfite, thiosulfate, S0) were each added with every defined and undefined substrate and none stimulated growth. Iron(III) not tested. Fumarate is both donor and acceptor (disproportionation to succinate + acetate); H2 is produced during fumarate growth (genome paper, BMC Genomics 2021) — H2 production, not oxidation. notes: HSL-3221T kept (all four Thiomicrolovo species are equally documented in the same paper/table). Name not validly published under ICNP; LPSN corrected spelling to 'Thiomicrolobovum sulfuroxydans' corrig. Cui et al. 2025. Internal inconsistency: genus description says donors include 'thiosulfate, sulfite, sulfide, and elemental sulfur', but species description/Table 1 give only thiosulfate and sulfide for HSL-3221T (sulfite/S0 then effectively negative for this strain but not explicitly stated). Sulfur disproportionation (thiosulfate/S0 with ferrihydrite as sulfide scavenger) reported positive for all strains incl. HSL-3221T - not captured by any category. Alternative-acceptor tests were run under 80% H2/20% CO2 in MMJHS medium (described as containing thiosulfate and H2 as energy sources), so thiosulfate was available as donor even though Thiomicrolovo cannot use H2; acceptor negatives are therefore interpretable. Sulfate as acceptor not listed in methods (Table 1 shows SO4(2-) for HSL3-7T only) -> not_tested. Isolated from mangrove sediments, Zhangzhou, China.
